bull_bear.body: Rights Issue of INR 364cr planned for R-32 plant; Promoter to subscribe proportionately (including conversion of interest-free loan); No further equity dilution expected post-rights; Debt-free stance maintained.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: 1) Commissioning delays (Khalapur helium delayed 3 months due to pressure upgrade to 300 bar; Mambatu re-engineered for larger scale); 2) Execution risk on rapid capex deployment; 3) Raw material volatility (imported helium/components); 4) Regulatory changes in fluorocarbons.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on long-term structural shift to manufacturing; Defensive on communication gaps regarding delays (cites 're-engineering' for better economics); Aggressive on margin expansion and market share capture.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Promoter's 2% stake sale was a bridge to fund R-32 kickstart after market volatility killed a preferential issue; R-32 capacity doubled mid-stream (5k to 10k MT) to avoid future shutdowns for expansion, signaling a 'big bang' manufacturing entry rather than phased learning.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Pan-India footprint of four manufacturing facilities enabling efficient product availability and reliable supply across key industrial clusters
- Technical expertise in customized gas blending and value-added, application-specific processing rather than commodity refrigerant supply
- Diversified portfolio of over 40 gases serving more than 200 customers across more than 15 industry segments, limiting single-sector dependence
- More than three decades of industry expertise through legacy operations in processing, debulking, blending, storage and distribution
- Technology collaboration with Portugal-based SYS ADVANCE for helium recovery and liquefaction systems
- Long-term liquid helium sourcing partnership with Sharjah Oxygen Company (Dubai) drawing on RAS Gases & Oilfields, Qatar
- In-house laboratory testing, modern filling systems and safety protocols supporting quality assurance
- Backward integration into R-32 manufacture expected to strengthen raw material security
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Regulatory transition away from high-GWP refrigerants — Growing regulatory focus on greenhouse gas emissions and initiatives such as the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol are accelerating the shift to low-GWP refrigerants; the MD&A flags that investments required for developing low-GWP technologies and evolving environmental regulations present certain challenges for the industry.
- Raw material and commodity cost volatility — The MD&A names raw material cost volatility as an important industry consideration and cites World Bank expectations of overall commodity prices rising approximately 22% during 2026 with Brent averaging US$94 per barrel, which it says continues to impact manufacturing, logistics, transportation, chemicals, refrigeration and industrial production.
- Foreign currency exchange rate exposure — The Company enters into sale and purchase transactions denominated in foreign currencies, so exposures to exchange rate fluctuations arise; part of the foreign-currency monetary position is not hedged by derivative instruments and management relies on monitoring plus remedial hedging measures.
- Interest rate risk on variable-rate borrowings — The Company states it is mainly exposed to interest rate risk due to its variable interest rate borrowings, the risk arising from uncertainty about future market interest rates on those borrowings.
- Credit and concentration risk on receivables — Credit risk covers direct default, deterioration of creditworthiness and concentration risk, principally on cash and bank balances, trade receivables, finance receivables and loans and advances; mitigation is quarterly receivable review, credit-limit review and a diverse customer base.
- Liquidity risk on meeting financial obligations — The Company identifies liquidity risk as the risk that it cannot meet its financial obligations, managed through fund and non-fund based working capital lines from various banks and by investing surplus funds in bank fixed deposits.
- Execution risk on the shift from distribution to manufacturing — The Company is moving from gas processing and distribution into manufacturing via the 10,000 MT R-32 facility at Bhilwara, a proposed approximately Rs 200 crore HFO facility with construction targeted for 2027, and new facilities at Khalapur and Mambattu; this is a step change in capital intensity and no commissioning or ramp dates are disclosed in the bundle.
- Geopolitical and supply chain disruption affecting imported inputs and helium — The Company sources liquid helium through a partnership with Sharjah Oxygen Company, Dubai, from RAS Gases & Oilfields, Qatar; the MD&A separately notes that conflict in the Middle East significantly disrupted energy supply routes and global commodity flows, raising shipping and production costs across industries.
- Contingent tax and guarantee exposures — The Company discloses matters with Income Tax Authorities on which it has preferred appeals pending with various appellate authorities, and outstanding performance bank guarantees issued to customs against import transactions; the performance guarantee facility is 100% secured against a term deposit of Mr. Shazad Rustomji, a promoter-director.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Refrigerants: R-32 backward integration (10k MT Bhilwara); Specialty Gases: Helium liquefaction/recovery (Khalapur & Mambatu), HFO blending; High-Purity: Semiconductor/Defense applications via SYS Advanced tie-up.

business.body:
- [Guidance] Chairman's letter and Way Forward section state management expects 30-35% revenue CAGR over the next 3 years while maintaining sustainable margins, and targets a ~3-4% EBITDA/profitability margin improvement over the medium term from backward integration and higher-value products (e.g., semiconductor gases) - explicitly flagged by the deck as forward-looking, not established fact.
- [Helium sourcing deal] Long-term strategic sourcing partnership with Sharjah Oxygen Company L.L.C. (SOC), sourcing liquid helium from RAS Gases & Oilfields, Qatar, targets semiconductor/electronics, healthcare (MRI/medical imaging), aerospace & defense, and fiber-optics end markets.
- [Industry sizing, third-party sources] Deck cites the global fluorochemicals market at USD 76.7bn (2025) growing to USD 204.4bn by 2035 (10.3% CAGR, Future Market Insights) and the India fluorochemicals market at ~USD 750mn (2025) growing at ~10.5% CAGR through 2034 (marknteladvisors/Thereportcubes) - external estimates, not company data.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Transition from a refrigerant gas processor and distributor into an integrated fluorochemicals and specialty gases platform
- Backward integration into fluorochemical manufacturing, starting with the proposed 10,000 MT R-32 facility at Bhilwara, Rajasthan, to strengthen raw material security and improve operational efficiencies
- Build domestic capability in next-generation low-GWP refrigerants through a proposed HFO manufacturing facility at Bhilwara (Hurda), Rajasthan under an MoU with the Government of Rajasthan
- Expand in specialty and semiconductor gases and strengthen the pan-India manufacturing footprint through upcoming facilities at Khalapur and Mambattu
- Build helium capability through a technology collaboration with Portugal-based SYS ADVANCE for helium recovery and liquefaction systems, targeting space, defence and other high-precision industries
- Secure global helium supply via a long-term partnership with Sharjah Oxygen Company, Dubai, for sourcing liquid helium from RAS Gases & Oilfields, Qatar
- Compete through customized gas blending and value-added, application-specific processing rather than conventional refrigerant supply
- Deploy IPO proceeds and a strengthened capital base into manufacturing infrastructure, technology partnerships and next-generation fluorochemicals
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY2025-26 was the year Stallion began converting from an asset-light gas processing and distribution model into a manufacturing platform. The Company commenced development of its proposed 10,000 MT R-32 manufacturing facility at Bhilwara, Rajasthan after receiving Environmental Clearance; this is described as its first major backward integration initiative, expected to strengthen raw material security, improve operational efficiencies and enhance long-term competitiveness. The next phase is a hydrofluoroolefin (HFO) manufacturing facility at Bhilwara (Hurda), Rajasthan, covered by a Memorandum of Understanding signed with the Government of Rajasthan; the proposed investment is approximately Rs 200 crore with construction targeted to commence in 2027, following the planned commissioning of the R-32 project. Alongside these, the Company is building a semiconductor and specialty gas debulking and blending facility at Khalapur, Maharashtra and a refrigerant debulking and blending facility at Mambattu, Andhra Pradesh, and has acquired land at Bhilwara, Rajasthan. Capability is also being added through partnerships rather than plants: a technology collaboration with Portugal-based SYS ADVANCE for helium recovery and liquefaction systems, and a long-term liquid helium sourcing partnership with Sharjah Oxygen Company, Dubai, drawing on RAS Gases & Oilfields, Qatar. The existing footprint remains four facilities at Khalapur and Panvel (Maharashtra), Ghiloth (Rajasthan) and Manesar (Haryana). Funding comes from the IPO completed during the year, which the Directors' Report says strengthened the capital base; members approved by postal ballot a variation in the terms of the objects of the IPO issue. No commissioning or ramp date is disclosed for the R-32 facility.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management attributes FY26 revenue growth to higher sales volumes, an improving product mix and sustained demand across multiple end-user industries
- Regulatory transition toward low-GWP refrigerants, driven by the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol, is accelerating adoption of HFOs, ammonia, carbon dioxide and blended refrigerants in India
- Expanding domestic electronics manufacturing, telecom investment and semiconductor-related activity are expected to accelerate fluorochemical adoption in that segment
- Pharmaceutical and healthcare demand for fluorinated intermediates and advanced fluorination technologies is described as an emerging growth opportunity
- Refrigeration and air-conditioning remain one of the largest application segments, supported by urbanisation, cold-chain infrastructure and climate-control demand
- The Indian fluorochemicals market is cited as growing at a CAGR of around 10.24% during 2024-2029 (MarkNtel Advisors), with the global market at a 4.46% CAGR (Fortune Business Insights)
- Government programmes such as Make in India and the PLI Scheme are cited as expanding the industrial base and demand for fluorochemical products
- Management flags that investments required for low-GWP technologies and evolving environmental regulations present certain challenges, alongside raw material cost volatility
- Rising commodity prices — with the World Bank expecting overall commodity prices up approximately 22% in 2026 and Brent averaging US$94 per barrel — are cited as pressuring manufacturing, logistics and refrigeration costs globally
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Stallion is transitioning from a blender/distributor to an integrated manufacturer with a 10k MT R-32 plant (Aug '26) and expanded helium infrastructure, targeting a PAT margin jump from 10% to 24%. While FY26 guidance (INR 430cr Rev, INR 40cr PAT) remains intact, execution risks on capex funding (Rights Issue) and plant commissioning delays (Khalapur/Mambatu to Mar-Apr '26) are key near-term monitors.

currentContext.expansion: FY2025-26 was the year Stallion began converting from an asset-light gas processing and distribution model into a manufacturing platform. The Company commenced development of its proposed 10,000 MT R-32 manufacturing facility at Bhilwara, Rajasthan after receiving Environmental Clearance; this is described as its first major backward integration initiative, expected to strengthen raw material security, improve operational efficiencies and enhance long-term competitiveness. The next phase is a hydrofluoroolefin (HFO) manufacturing facility at Bhilwara (Hurda), Rajasthan, covered by a Memorandum of Understanding signed with the Government of Rajasthan; the proposed investment is approximately Rs 200 crore with construction targeted to commence in 2027, following the planned commissioning of the R-32 project. Alongside these, the Company is building a semiconductor and specialty gas debulking and blending facility at Khalapur, Maharashtra and a refrigerant debulking and blending facility at Mambattu, Andhra Pradesh, and has acquired land at Bhilwara, Rajasthan. Capability is also being added through partnerships rather than plants: a technology collaboration with Portugal-based SYS ADVANCE for helium recovery and liquefaction systems, and a long-term liquid helium sourcing partnership with Sharjah Oxygen Company, Dubai, drawing on RAS Gases & Oilfields, Qatar. The existing footprint remains four facilities at Khalapur and Panvel (Maharashtra), Ghiloth (Rajasthan) and Manesar (Haryana). Funding comes from the IPO completed during the year, which the Directors' Report says strengthened the capital base; members approved by postal ballot a variation in the terms of the objects of the IPO issue. No commissioning or ramp date is disclosed for the R-32 facility.

risks.risk: Regulatory transition away from high-GWP refrigerants
risks.note: Growing regulatory focus on greenhouse gas emissions and initiatives such as the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol are accelerating the shift to low-GWP refrigerants; the MD&A flags that investments required for developing low-GWP technologies and evolving environmental regulations present certain challenges for the industry.

risks.risk: Raw material and commodity cost volatility
risks.note: The MD&A names raw material cost volatility as an important industry consideration and cites World Bank expectations of overall commodity prices rising approximately 22% during 2026 with Brent averaging US$94 per barrel, which it says continues to impact manufacturing, logistics, transportation, chemicals, refrigeration and industrial production.

The Company enters into sale and purchase transactions denominated in foreign currencies, so exposures to exchange rate fluctuations arise; part of the foreign-currency monetary position is not hedged by derivative instruments and management relies on monitoring plus remedial hedging measures.

risks.risk: Interest rate risk on variable-rate borrowings
risks.note: The Company states it is mainly exposed to interest rate risk due to its variable interest rate borrowings, the risk arising from uncertainty about future market interest rates on those borrowings.

risks.risk: Credit and concentration risk on receivables
risks.note: Credit risk covers direct default, deterioration of creditworthiness and concentration risk, principally on cash and bank balances, trade receivables, finance receivables and loans and advances; mitigation is quarterly receivable review, credit-limit review and a diverse customer base.

risks.risk: Liquidity risk on meeting financial obligations
risks.note: The Company identifies liquidity risk as the risk that it cannot meet its financial obligations, managed through fund and non-fund based working capital lines from various banks and by investing surplus funds in bank fixed deposits.

risks.risk: Execution risk on the shift from distribution to manufacturing
risks.note: The Company is moving from gas processing and distribution into manufacturing via the 10,000 MT R-32 facility at Bhilwara, a proposed approximately Rs 200 crore HFO facility with construction targeted for 2027, and new facilities at Khalapur and Mambattu; this is a step change in capital intensity and no commissioning or ramp dates are disclosed in the bundle.

risks.risk: Geopolitical and supply chain disruption affecting imported inputs and helium
risks.note: The Company sources liquid helium through a partnership with Sharjah Oxygen Company, Dubai, from RAS Gases & Oilfields, Qatar; the MD&A separately notes that conflict in the Middle East significantly disrupted energy supply routes and global commodity flows, raising shipping and production costs across industries.

The Company discloses matters with Income Tax Authorities on which it has preferred appeals pending with various appellate authorities, and outstanding performance bank guarantees issued to customs against import transactions; the performance guarantee facility is 100% secured against a term deposit of Mr. Shazad Rustomji, a promoter-director.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Stallion India Fluorochemicals is a pan-India processor, blender and distributor of refrigerant, specialty and industrial gases, now transitioning into an integrated fluorochemicals and specialty gases manufacturing platform.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Incorporated in 2002, the Company undertakes processing, debulking, blending, storage and distribution of refrigerant, specialty and industrial gases from four manufacturing facilities in Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Haryana. It supplies over 40 gases including HFCs, HFOs, hydrocarbons, specialty gases, semiconductor gases and high-purity industrial gases to more than 200 customers across over 15 industry segments. Its stated differentiator is customized gas blending and value-added, application-specific processing rather than conventional refrigerant supply.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Management attributes FY26 revenue growth to higher sales volumes, an improving product mix and sustained demand across multiple end-user industries
- Regulatory transition toward low-GWP refrigerants, driven by the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol, is accelerating adoption of HFOs, ammonia, carbon dioxide and blended refrigerants in India
- Expanding domestic electronics manufacturing, telecom investment and semiconductor-related activity are expected to accelerate fluorochemical adoption in that segment
- Pharmaceutical and healthcare demand for fluorinated intermediates and advanced fluorination technologies is described as an emerging growth opportunity
- Refrigeration and air-conditioning remain one of the largest application segments, supported by urbanisation, cold-chain infrastructure and climate-control demand
- The Indian fluorochemicals market is cited as growing at a CAGR of around 10.24% during 2024-2029 (MarkNtel Advisors), with the global market at a 4.46% CAGR (Fortune Business Insights)
- Government programmes such as Make in India and the PLI Scheme are cited as expanding the industrial base and demand for fluorochemical products
- Management flags that investments required for low-GWP technologies and evolving environmental regulations present certain challenges, alongside raw material cost volatility
- Rising commodity prices — with the World Bank expecting overall commodity prices up approximately 22% in 2026 and Brent averaging US$94 per barrel — are cited as pressuring manufacturing, logistics and refrigeration costs globally

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Current PAT margin ~10%; Target PAT margin 24% for new products (R-32, Helium); Cost competitiveness via backward integration and economies of scale (doubled R-32 capacity from 5k to 10k MT).

capital_allocation.body: Rights Issue of INR 364cr planned for R-32 plant; Promoter to subscribe proportionately (including conversion of interest-free loan); No further equity dilution expected post-rights; Debt-free stance maintained.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: FY2025-26 was the year Stallion began converting from an asset-light gas processing and distribution model into a manufacturing platform. The Company commenced development of its proposed 10,000 MT R-32 manufacturing facility at Bhilwara, Rajasthan after receiving Environmental Clearance; this is described as its first major backward integration initiative, expected to strengthen raw material security, improve operational efficiencies and enhance long-term competitiveness. The next phase is a hydrofluoroolefin (HFO) manufacturing facility at Bhilwara (Hurda), Rajasthan, covered by a Memorandum of Understanding signed with the Government of Rajasthan; the proposed investment is approximately Rs 200 crore with construction targeted to commence in 2027, following the planned commissioning of the R-32 project. Alongside these, the Company is building a semiconductor and specialty gas debulking and blending facility at Khalapur, Maharashtra and a refrigerant debulking and blending facility at Mambattu, Andhra Pradesh, and has acquired land at Bhilwara, Rajasthan. Capability is also being added through partnerships rather than plants: a technology collaboration with Portugal-based SYS ADVANCE for helium recovery and liquefaction systems, and a long-term liquid helium sourcing partnership with Sharjah Oxygen Company, Dubai, drawing on RAS Gases & Oilfields, Qatar. The existing footprint remains four facilities at Khalapur and Panvel (Maharashtra), Ghiloth (Rajasthan) and Manesar (Haryana). Funding comes from the IPO completed during the year, which the Directors' Report says strengthened the capital base; members approved by postal ballot a variation in the terms of the objects of the IPO issue. No commissioning or ramp date is disclosed for the R-32 facility.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident on long-term structural shift to manufacturing; Defensive on communication gaps regarding delays (cites 're-engineering' for better economics); Aggressive on margin expansion and market share capture.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Pan-India footprint of four manufacturing facilities enabling efficient product availability and reliable supply across key industrial clusters
- Technical expertise in customized gas blending and value-added, application-specific processing rather than commodity refrigerant supply
- Diversified portfolio of over 40 gases serving more than 200 customers across more than 15 industry segments, limiting single-sector dependence
- More than three decades of industry expertise through legacy operations in processing, debulking, blending, storage and distribution
- Technology collaboration with Portugal-based SYS ADVANCE for helium recovery and liquefaction systems
- Long-term liquid helium sourcing partnership with Sharjah Oxygen Company (Dubai) drawing on RAS Gases & Oilfields, Qatar
- In-house laboratory testing, modern filling systems and safety protocols supporting quality assurance
- Backward integration into R-32 manufacture expected to strengthen raw material security

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: 1) Commissioning delays (Khalapur helium delayed 3 months due to pressure upgrade to 300 bar; Mambatu re-engineered for larger scale); 2) Execution risk on rapid capex deployment; 3) Raw material volatility (imported helium/components); 4) Regulatory changes in fluorocarbons.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Promoter's 2% stake sale was a bridge to fund R-32 kickstart after market volatility killed a preferential issue; R-32 capacity doubled mid-stream (5k to 10k MT) to avoid future shutdowns for expansion, signaling a 'big bang' manufacturing entry rather than phased learning.

other.body:
- [Guidance] Chairman's letter and Way Forward section state management expects 30-35% revenue CAGR over the next 3 years while maintaining sustainable margins, and targets a ~3-4% EBITDA/profitability margin improvement over the medium term from backward integration and higher-value products (e.g., semiconductor gases) - explicitly flagged by the deck as forward-looking, not established fact.

themes.title: Import-substitution / China+1 specialty chemicals
themes.need: After the worst agrochem/chemicals year in living memory, the cycle is turning on China+1 reshoring and global pigment/dye consolidation. SUDARSCHEM is now #2 global pigment player post-Heubach; SUMICHEM posted record FY26 margins; AETHER/ANURAS/DEEPAKNTR/CLEAN add CRAMS + backward-integration; war-driven RM/freight inflation is being passed through. Q1FY27 shows the reshoring build-out actually landing: HSCL grew consolidated revenue 28% to INR 1,432cr with PAT INR 228cr (+27%) at a 22% EBITDA margin while opening three new value ladders in a single quarter (carbon nanotube 200 MTPA by Q4FY27, super-speciality carbon black 6,000 MTPA by FY28, and India's first commercial anthraquinone/carbazole plant), all self-funded with no incremental debt; TATVA grew revenue 43% YoY and delivered its first commercial-plant-scale semiconductor batch, qualified by the customer and called 'the glaring achievement of the past decade' (though commercialisation is explicitly not before Q4 CY2028); FCL tripled total income to INR 386.72cr (+165%) with Texas capacity nearly doubled to 148,000 MTPA and already running 63% on a single shift, so its next revenue leg needs only USD 1-2mn of capex.
themes.driver: Volume rebound as destocking ends; price hikes sticking; new value-ladder commissioning (HSCL CNT/carbon black) and semiconductor-materials qualification (TATVA).

themes.title: Industrial gases, chlor-alkali & commodity chemicals
themes.need: A capacity-led commodity-chemical and industrial-gas cycle underpins the basic-materials chain - ELLEN on air-separation/industrial gases; EPIGRAL/CHEMPLASTS/DCW/DCMSHRIRAM/GHCL/TATACHEM/GNFC on chlor-alkali, soda-ash and vinyls; LORDSCHLO on caustic; CHEMBONDCH on water-treatment chemicals. Pricing/utilization and energy costs are the near-term swing factors.
themes.driver: Caustic/soda-ash price recovery; utilization ramp on new capacity; energy-cost relief.
